Real Good Foods is a US frozen food company, run from Cherry Hill, New Jersey with roots in Los Angeles, selling lower-carb, high-protein frozen meals and snacks such as cauliflower-crust pizza, stuffed chicken, breakfast sandwiches and burritos under the Real Good Foods brand, in major US grocery chains and Costco. It listed on Nasdaq (RGF) in 2021 and entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2025 with a sale of its assets. Known US supermarket brand with moderate recognition.

Apical Group is a Singapore-based oleochemicals and palm oil company, a unit of the Royal Golden Eagle Group, controlled by Indonesian businessman Sukanto Tanoto. It processes palm oil and kernel at refineries in Indonesia and China, producing cooking oil, biodiesel, fatty acids and specialty fats, selling to food manufacturers and traders in over 60 countries. Raised about 750 million dollars through loans. Private group, with B2B profile and some environmental criticism. Low consumer awareness.

Dhanani Group is a Sugar Land, Texas family business that became one of the largest US quick-service restaurant franchisees, operating hundreds of Wendy's, Popeyes, Carl's Jr. and Burger King outlets, along with real estate and fuel stations. It was founded by Shamoon Dhanani in Houston. Recorded funding is about 500 million dollars. Privately held. Customers are consumers via the franchised brands, with the Dhanani name mostly known within the franchising industry.

La Colombe Coffee Roasters is a Philadelphia-founded coffee roaster and beverage company, shown with a Los Angeles office, known for its Draft Latte canned cold coffee, bottled cold brew, whole bean coffee and cafes across US cities. Founded in 1994 by Todd Carmichael and JP Iberti, it was acquired by Chobani in 2023 for about 900 million dollars, having earlier received an investment from Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya. Wide US retail and cafe presence. Strong consumer brand.

GOOD Meat is a San Francisco-based cultivated meat company, a division of Eat Just, which makes cultured chicken grown from animal cells, and was the first to win regulatory approval for sale, in Singapore in 2020 and in the US in 2023. Its products are sold in a few restaurants and, in Singapore, in retail as a blended product. Recorded funding is about 267 million dollars. Privately held. Early stage consumer food brand, with scaled-back operations since 2023.

Seek Pet Foods is a Chinese pet food manufacturer based in Linyi, Shandong, working on an OEM and ODM basis for dog and cat food brands and also producing its own products. Recorded funding is about 1.57 billion yuan. Customers are pet brands and retailers in China and exports. Its ownership and scale are not confirmed here. B2B manufacturer with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

George Weston Limited is a Toronto-based Canadian holding company, controlled by the Weston family, which owns about 52 percent of Loblaw Companies, Canada's largest food retailer and pharmacy operator (Loblaws, Shoppers Drug Mart, No Frills, President's Choice), and a stake in Choice Properties REIT. It sold its Weston Foods bakery business in 2021. Revenue is about 60 billion Canadian dollars. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (WN). Parent brand is little known, though its retail brands are household names.

Lelecha is a Chinese fresh-tea drink and bakery chain based in Shanghai, selling milk tea and tea-based drinks paired with soft European-style bread bags, through a few hundred directly operated and franchised shops across China. Customers are young urban consumers who buy at mid-range prices. Recorded funding is about 194 million dollars. Privately held. Consumer brand with strong regional visibility in China's competitive tea chain market and a young female fan base.

Its brands, plants, ownership and scale are not confirmed here, though the sector points to chicken and related products sold to consumers and food service buyers in Saudi Arabia. Likely a regional food producer with limited consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Real Pet Food Company is an Australian pet food business based in Crows Nest, New South Wales, producing natural and ethically sourced dog and cat food, with brands such as Ivory Coat and Black Hawk sold through supermarkets, pet stores and online. Recorded funding is about 248 million Australian dollars. Privately held. Mass-market pet brand with good Australian retail presence. Ownership and scale are not fully confirmed here.

about: The Simply Good Foods Company is a Denver-based consumer packaged goods firm that markets nutritional snacks and meal replacements under the Atkins, Quest and OWYN brands, sold through grocery, mass, club and online channels in North America and internationally. Revenue is about 1.3 billion dollars. It was formed in 2017 through a SPAC merger and is listed on Nasdaq (SMPL). Strong health and fitness-oriented consumer brands, widely available in US supermarkets and with sports sponsorship history.

Sao Martinho is a Brazilian sugar and ethanol producer based in Pradopolis, Sao Paulo state, which grinds sugarcane at four mills, producing sugar, ethanol, bioelectricity and biogas, and exports to many countries. Customers are food producers, fuel distributors and power buyers. Revenue is about 6 billion reais. It is listed on B3 (SMTO3) and controlled by the Ometto family. B2B agribusiness brand with limited consumer awareness.

Above Food is a Canadian plant-based and alternative protein company based in Regina, Saskatchewan, producing pea and lentil protein ingredients, pasta, and consumer food products, along with a plant-based brand called Above Food. It listed on Nasdaq (ABVE) in 2024 after a SPAC merger with Bite Acquisition Corp. Customers are retailers and food manufacturers. Recorded funding is about 60 million dollars. Small food brand with limited consumer awareness.

Black Rock Coffee Bar is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based drive-thru and neighbourhood coffee chain with over 150 shops across the western US, particularly Oregon, Washington, California, Texas and Arizona, selling espresso, cold drinks, tea and pastries. Founded in 2008 in Portland, Oregon, it is known for its community coffee culture. It is listed on Nasdaq (BRCB) after a 2025 IPO. Recorded funding is about 75 million dollars. Regional consumer brand with growing awareness.

Fine Foods & Pharmaceuticals NTM (FF) is an Italian contract development and manufacturing company in Bergamo, producing pharmaceutical and nutraceutical products such as tablets, powders and capsules for pharma and health brands. It is listed on Euronext Milan. Recorded funding is about 30 million euros. B2B manufacturer with no consumer awareness. Its exact ownership and scale are not fully confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Chilean salmon producer based in Puerto Montt that breeds, farms, processes and exports Atlantic salmon, selling fresh and frozen fillets to customers in the US, Brazil, Japan and elsewhere. Listed on the Santiago stock exchange (MULTI X). One of the largest salmon farmers in Chile. Funding of about $290 million shown. B2B food exporter with limited consumer brand awareness, mainly through retailer private labels.

Icelandic seafood company based in Reykjavik, formerly HB Grandi, that operates fishing vessels and processing plants and sells frozen and fresh fish, mostly cod, saithe and pelagic species, to customers in Europe and Asia. One of Iceland's largest fisheries groups by quota. Listed on Nasdaq Iceland. Funding of about ISK 33 billion shown. B2B food exporter with strong recognition in Iceland, little brand presence abroad.

Paraguayan beef packer and exporter based around Concepcion, with a main office in Asuncion, slaughtering cattle and selling beef cuts to export markets including Chile, Russia, Taiwan and the Middle East. Total funding of about $161 million shown. B2B meat processor with strong local profile in Paraguay's cattle industry but little consumer brand outside the country. Exports are central to its business, and it competes with other Paraguayan packers in a market that is among the largest beef exporters in South America.

about: Siniora Food Industries is a Jordanian processed meat and food manufacturer based in Amman, known for the Siniora brand of sausages, frankfurters, burgers, ham, deli meats and ready meals, sold in Jordan, the Gulf, Iraq, Palestine and other Middle East markets. Customers are retailers, restaurants and households, and the company earns revenue from branded food sales through its own distribution network. Crunchbase shows $80 million in funding, latest in March 2024, and flags it as listed. Strong consumer brand visibility across the Levant, with limited reach outside the region.

Steakholder Foods, formerly MeaTech 3D, is an Israeli food technology company based in Rehovot, developing cultivated meat and fish and 3D bioprinting technology, and selling plant-based premixes and printers. It supplies food producers and licenses technology rather than selling to consumers directly, with partners in Europe and Asia including Umami Bioworks. It is listed on Nasdaq under STKH. Crunchbase shows about $41 million in funding, latest in July 2026. Pre-commercial alternative protein firm with small revenue and modest public awareness.

Sill Entreprises is a privately held French food and consumer goods producer based in Plouvien, in Brittany, according to Crunchbase, with funding of 393 million shown for 2014. The input does not list its products or brands, and the investor figure is undefined as to currency. Its customers are probably French retailers and consumers. Details on ownership, brand names and size cannot be confirmed from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Del Taco is a US quick-service Mexican-American restaurant chain, based in Lake Forest, California, founded in 1964, selling tacos, burritos, fries and shakes at roughly 600 restaurants, mostly in California and the western US. It listed on Nasdaq in 2015 via a SPAC with Levy Acquisition, and Jack in the Box bought it in 2022 for about $585 million. Customers are fast-food consumers. Familiar regional consumer brand in the western US.

Kopi Kenangan is an Indonesian coffee chain, based in Jakarta, founded in 2017 by Edy Tjahyadi and James Prananto, selling grab-and-go coffee, iced milk coffee and snacks through over 1,000 outlets and delivery apps. It raised a $96 million Series C in December 2021 at a valuation of about $1 billion, with investors including Alpha JWC and Sequoia India. It has expanded across Indonesia with an extensive store network. Strong consumer brand in Indonesia, little recognition elsewhere.

MOD Pizza is a US fast-casual pizza chain, founded in 2008 in Seattle and based in Bellevue, Washington, offering build-your-own individual pizzas and salads at around 500 restaurants at its peak. It went through a bankruptcy sale in 2024 after financial difficulties, and many sites were closed. Customers are fast-casual diners across the US. Consumer chain with notable awareness in Washington state and the western US.

JDB Group is the Chinese company behind the Jiaduobao herbal tea brand, a red-can cooling herbal tea that became a leading beverage in China after a long trademark dispute over the Wong Lo Kat (Wanglaoji) name with Guangzhou Pharmaceutical. Based in Beijing, it sells beverages through distributors and retailers across China. Funding of about CNY 2 billion is shown for 2017. Very strong consumer brand recognition in China, though it lost market share after the dispute.

Pagoda (Baiguoyuan) is a Chinese fruit retail chain, based in Shenzhen, founded in 2001, which operates thousands of stores selling fresh fruit across the country, supplied by its own sourcing. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023 (2411), with Crunchbase showing CNY 1.9 billion raised by 2018. Customers are Chinese urban households. Strong consumer recognition in China, with limited reach outside.

Fresh Easy is a South Korean meal kit and food distributor, based in Seoul, selling prepared ingredient kits and fresh food to consumers online. Crunchbase shows large funding of KRW 307 billion in November 2021. Customers are Korean households, and revenue comes from food sales and delivery. The input does not say who owns it or how large it is. Consumer food brand with limited recognition outside Korea.
cb_desc: Fresh Easy is a distributor of meal kits.

about: OTG is a US airport concessions operator, based in New York, best known for its tablet-ordering restaurants and shops at airport terminals such as JFK, LaGuardia and Newark, run under brands like CIBO Express. Customers are travellers at airports, paying for food, beverages and retail. Funding of $250 million is shown for September 2016. Privately held. Recognised by frequent travellers in New York, with little wider consumer profile.

about: Naixuecha (Nayuki) is a Chinese premium tea drink chain, based in Shenzhen, founded in 2015, selling fruit teas and bakery items through more than 1,000 stores and its app. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2021 (2150), and raised about $216 million before that. Customers are young urban Chinese consumers. Strong consumer brand in China, with little reach outside.

Olo is a SaaS platform for restaurant digital ordering and delivery. Its Ordering, Dispatch, Rails and Engage products let chains such as Five Guys, Wingstop and Subway take online orders, handle third-party delivery, and run loyalty and marketing, with revenue from subscription and transaction fees. Based in New York and founded in 2005, it listed on the NYSE in 2021 (OLO) and was taken private by Thoma Bravo in a roughly $2 billion deal announced in 2025. Serves tens of thousands of restaurant locations. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Olam is a Singapore-headquartered agri-business that sources, processes and supplies food ingredients, spices, vegetables, coffee, cocoa, edible nuts and other agricultural products, now organised mainly into ofi (Olam Food Ingredients) and Olam Agri. Crunchbase's text refers to its spices and vegetable ingredients business, including dehydrated onion. Customers are global food and beverage makers and traders. Founded in 1989, it operates across dozens of countries and is controlled by Temasek-linked shareholders and listed in Singapore. Mostly B2B, with limited consumer brand visibility.

about: LT Foods is an Indian packaged foods group, based in Gurugram, best known for basmati rice brands including Daawat, Royal and Heritage, as well as organic foods, ready-to-eat meals and convenience foods. It sells in India and in more than 80 countries, to retailers and consumers, and earns from branded product sales. Founded in 1990 and listed on the NSE and BSE. Household name in India for premium basmati rice and well known in diaspora markets such as the US, Middle East and Europe.

Once Upon a Farm is a Berkeley, California organic baby and kids food brand, co-founded by actress Jennifer Garner, selling refrigerated cold-pressed pouches, snacks, oat bars and smoothies for children, in grocery stores like Whole Foods, Target and Costco, plus online. It earns from retail sales. Crunchbase shows about $117 million in funding, with the latest round in 2022, and flags it as a listed company. Strong US consumer brand among parents, supported by its celebrity link.

Zabka Group is the operator of Poland's largest convenience store network, Zabka, with more than 10,000 small neighbourhood stores, plus the Freshmarket concept and the Jush! digital services, and a growing presence in Romania. It sells groceries, ready meals and services such as parcel pick-up to consumers, and earns from retail margins and franchise operations. Registered in Luxembourg and majority backed by CVC, it listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange in 2025. Very high consumer recognition in Poland.

Bikaji Foods is an Indian snacks company, based in Bikaner, Rajasthan, which makes and sells bhujia, namkeen, packaged sweets, papad and other ethnic snacks under the Bikaji brand, in India and abroad, through distributors and retailers. Founded in 1993, it is listed on the NSE and BSE after an IPO in November 2022. Recognised household snack brand in northern and western India, competing with Haldiram's, with growing exports.

Foods & Inns is a Mumbai-based Indian food processing company, listed on the NSE and BSE, with a business in fruit pulp, vegetable and processed food products, along with hospitality and real estate interests. Customers are food manufacturers and other businesses, and consumers through some products. Crunchbase shows about INR 2.1 billion in funding, with the latest round in November 2022. Small-cap B2B brand, with limited consumer visibility.

Hatsun Agro Product is an Indian dairy company, based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, selling milk, curd, ice cream and dairy products under brands such as Arun Ice Creams, Arokya, Hatsun and Ibaco, through a large network of milk collection routes and retail outlets. It sources milk from farmers across southern India and has a growing presence elsewhere. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Strong consumer brands in South India, notably Arokya milk and Arun ice creams.

Utz Brands is a Hanover, Pennsylvania snack food company, listed on the NYSE (UTZ), that makes and sells salty snacks including Utz potato chips and pretzels, Zapp's, Golden Flake, Boulder Canyon, Hawaiian Brand and ON THE BORDER tortilla chips, through supermarkets, convenience stores and distributors in the United States. Founded in 1921, it is the leading regional snack maker in several parts of the country. Strong consumer brand recognition, particularly in the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast.

Red Lobster is a US casual dining chain, based in Orlando, Florida, known for seafood such as Cheddar Bay Biscuits, shrimp and lobster, with about 500 restaurants in the US and Canada. It was owned by Darden, then Golden Gate Capital, then Thai Union, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2024 after losses, emerging in September 2024 owned by its lenders led by Fortress. Revenue is from restaurant sales. Household consumer brand across the US.
